description: Among rural Nigerian women, two-month prevalence was 58% for low back pain, 30% for neck and shoulder pain and 30% for elbow, hand and wrist pain. Women who appraised their domestic responsibilities as very stressful had significantly higher odds: OR 2.88 for low back pain, 4.58 for neck and shoulder pain, 1.88 for elbow, hand and wrist pain.
energy_note: Nearly three times the odds, for finding the housework stressful.

aspect: High demand and low control, specifically
description: The same study found high-demand/low-control conditions associated with higher low back pain odds at OR 2.58. That is the exact structure of unpaid domestic labour: the demands are fixed by others and the control is nil.
energy_note: Lots of demands, no authority, and it lands in the back.

aspect: The psychosocial factors outweighed the biomechanical ones
description: A population-based study in Nigeria found psychosocial factors the most important correlates of both self-reported and performance-based disability, while aggregate biomechanical exposure was not - though the authors flag a possible healthy-worker effect, since the rural population studied were all heavy manual workers.
energy_note: It is not only the lifting. It is the conditions around the lifting.

aspect: Which is the mechanism the brief was pointing at
description: PSY-004 describes the arithmetic that never stops. SOM-002 is the measured output of it. The load is not metaphorical and the link is in the peer-reviewed literature rather than asserted here.
energy_note: The stress, and the spine, in the same regression.

aspect: SCENARIO - the woman who is fine
description: Water from the borehole twice daily, forty litres. Firewood. Three children under seven. Her husband's mother, who is bedbound. She is thirty-four and has had back pain for four years and has never mentioned it to anyone, because everybody she knows has it.
energy_note: Four years of pain, unremarkable because it is universal.
